items.title: Feasibility, Safety, and Preliminary Effect Estimates of an Ultrasound-Informed Hybrid Joint-Sparing Rehabilitation Strategy in Patients With Rheumatoid Arthritis: A Prospective Non-Randomized Proof-of-Concept Study.
items.abstract: and PurposePhysical rehabilitation is recommended as an adjunct to pharmacological treatment in rheumatoid arthritis (RA); however, exercise prescription remains challenging when synovitis is active. Musculoskeletal ultrasonography (MSK-US), particularly power Doppler (PD), provides a sensitive assessment of synovial inflammatory activity and may help inform rehabilitation planning. The primary objectives were to describe the feasibility and safety of a 12-week ultrasound-informed hybrid joint-sparing rehabilitation protocol in patients with RA. Pain intensity (VAS) was the designated primary outcome for generating preliminary effect estimates, with ultrasonographic indices as secondary outcomes. No feasibility criteria were prespecified. This prospective non-randomized proof-of-concept study, reported according to the TREND statement, enroled 60 consecutive patients fulfiling the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria between February 2024 and January 2025. Participants were allocated by clinic attendance order (sequential recruitment) into a rehabilitation group (n = 30) or a control group (n = 30). The rehabilitation group received a 12-week ultrasound-informed hybrid protocol (supervised outpatient sessions plus a structured home programme) comprising weekly paraffin wax baths and baseline ultrasound-stratified exercise progression, alongside stable pharmacological therapy. Joint regions of the index (most affected) hand with baseline PD > 1 (68.9% of examined regions) were managed conservatively at programme initiation, with resistance loading deferred in favour of pain-free range-of-motion exercises. The control group received stable pharmacological therapy plus a single educational session. Pain was assessed using a 10-cm visual analogue scale (VAS). MSK-US of wrist, MCP, and PIP regions was performed at baseline and Week 12 using OMERACT semi-quantitative scoring. Feasibility outcomes (descriptive; no prespecified criteria) were: recruitment 60/60, retention 100%, supervised-session completion 12/12 after rescheduling, and home compliance 86%. In this unblinded, non-randomized comparison, pain reduction was greater in the rehabilitation group (ΔVAS: -2.88 ± 0.84 vs. -0.60 ± 0.20 cm; p < 0.001; Cohen's d = 3.74, 95% CI 2.90-4.58; between-group difference -2.27 cm, 95% CI -2.59 to -1.96; ANCOVA-adjusted difference -2.30, 95% CI -2.55 to -2.06; partial η 2  = 0.865); An improvement of ≥ 2.0 cm (exploratory threshold) occurred in 25/30 (83.3%) versus 0/30 (0%). The distributions of individual ΔVAS values showed no overlap between groups: the smallest improvement in the rehabilitation group (1.4 cm) exceeded the largest improvement in the control group (1.1 cm); control-group changes were unusually uniform and the effect size was probably overestimated. Between-group changes in total grey-scale synovitis (p = 0.327) and total PD (p = 0.340) were not statistically significant; no erosion progression was detected. No serious adverse events occurred; safety conclusions were limited to 12 weeks. Baseline DAS28 and VAS were comparable, although the rehabilitation group was older with longer disease duration and higher ESR. In this small, single-centre, non-randomized study, the protocol could be delivered as planned and no serious adverse events were observed over 12 weeks (no feasibility criteria were prespecified). Pain reduction was greater than with minimal education, but the difference is probably overestimated, may reflect non-specific effects of much greater therapist contact, and cannot be attributed to ultrasound-informed prescription; ultrasonographic synovitis and vascularity did not differ between groups. These preliminary, hypothesis-generating findings should inform, cautiously, the design of future randomized trials with active comparators.

items.title: Key genes in ferroptosis and oxidative stress pathways associated with ankylosing spondylitis.
items.abstract: This study investigated the expression profiles and clinical significance of oxidative stress-related genes (ORGs) and ferroptosis-related genes (FRGs) in peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) of patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS). The GSE73754 dataset was downloaded from GEO, and differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified and subsequently intersected with FRGs curated from the Driver, Suppressor, Marker, and Unclassified databases and ORGs retrieved from the MSigDB database. Functional enrichment (GO/KEGG) was performed, protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were constructed, and hub genes were identified using cytoHubba; the overlap of hub sets yielded seven key genes (G6PD, CYBB, TXNRD1, AKR1C3, MAP3K5, PARK7, and NFE2L2). Immune infiltration was estimated by ssGSEA, and key genes were validated by RT-qPCR in PBMCs from 113 AS patients (53 active, 60 stable), 48 rheumatoid arthritis patients, 24 osteoarthritis patients, and 50 healthy controls. We identified 44 differentially expressed FRGs and 40 differentially expressed ORGs enriched mainly in oxidative stress, lipid metabolism, and ferroptosis-related pathways; a four-gene nomogram was developed to predict AS risk. RT-qPCR confirmed the upregulation of G6PD and CYBB expression and the downregulation of the expression of TXNRD1, AKR1C3, MAP3K5, PARK7, and NFE2L2 in AS. Notably, G6PD levels were significantly higher in HLA-B27-positive patients. RT-qPCR analysis showed that G6PD had good diagnostic performance (AUC = 0.826), while CYBB expression was positively correlated with multiple inflammatory markers. Differentially expressed FRG and ORG play important roles in the pathogenesis of AS, with G6PD and CYBB potentially serving as potential AS-associated biomarkers.

items.title: Early EULAR Target Achievement and Kidney Outcomes in Lupus Nephritis.
items.abstract: The prognostic value of achieving the European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology (EULAR) 3- and 6-month treatment targets in lupus nephritis (LN) remains uncertain. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study of adults with biopsy-proven proliferative LN. Patients were classified by EULAR target achievement: a ≥ 25% reduction in urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) with preserved kidney function at 3 months and a ≥ 50% reduction in UPCR at 6 months. The primary outcome was a ≥ 30% decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) at 24 months from the higher of baseline or 3-month eGFR. Multivariable logistic regression and linear mixed-effects models were used. Among 449 screened patients, 293 and 288 constituted the 3- and 6-month analytic cohorts, respectively. For the 3-month EULAR target analysis, the primary outcome occurred in 24/213 (11.3%) achievers and 18/80 (22.5%) nonachievers (adjusted odds ratio [OR], 0.40; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.20-0.82). For the 6-month EULAR target analysis, the corresponding proportions were 31/246 (12.6%) and 11/42 (26.2%) (adjusted OR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.17-0.91). Adjusted eGFR trajectories were higher in achievers, although separation preceded 6-month classification. In a 3-month landmark analysis, the composite target showed no clear incremental association beyond kidney function at 3 months, whereas the UPCR-reduction criterion remained associated with subsequent eGFR decline (OR, 0.34; 95% CI, 0.14-0.86). Achievement of the EULAR early treatment targets at 3 and 6 months was associated with better kidney outcomes in proliferative LN. Achievement by 3 months may identify patients with a particularly favorable renal prognosis.

items.title: Leonurine microcomposite depots alleviate endometriosis and rheumatoid arthritis via shared anti-inflammatory cascades.
items.abstract: Chronic inflammatory diseases, such as endometriosis (EMS) and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), share a common pathogenic hallmark driven by a hyperinflammatory microenvironment. Nonetheless, long-acting therapeutic platforms capable of concurrently addressing these disparate disorders remain rarely explored. Herein, we developed a leonurine microcrystal-encapsulated microcomposite depot (Leo-micro@MD) capable of effectively mitigating inflammation, thereby reversing the progression of both EMS and RA. Systemic formulation optimization yielded an optimized Leo-micro@MD formulation with high drug loading and a sustained, burst-free release profile extending over 18 days, markedly reducing administration frequency. Mechanistically, Leo-micro@MD suppresses key upstream inflammatory cytokines, thereby branching into distinct downstream therapeutic pathways tailored to each disorder. In EMS, this reduction attenuated estrogen-ERα signaling and restored progesterone receptor B (PRB) expression, subsequently reactivating LC3B-mediated autophagy and Bax/Bcl-2-dependent apoptosis to eradicate ectopic lesions. Concurrently, in an adjuvant-induced arthritis rat model, this anti-inflammatory cascade attenuates synovial hyperplasia, rescues bone mineral density and trabecular architecture, and re-establishes articular matrix homeostasis, as confirmed by micro-CT and comprehensive histopathology. Importantly, these disease-modifying effects are achieved with an excellent systemic safety profile, with no detectable hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, or immune organ damage. Collectively, this study provides a robust and translatable controlled-release strategy for the comprehensive management of chronic inflammatory diseases.

items.title: Exploratory single-cell multiomics suggests naive CD4 + T cell dysregulation in treatment refractory rheumatoid arthritis.
items.abstract: Around 20% of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) have disease that remains refractory to multiple targeted treatments, highlighting a major clinical challenge. We determine single-nucleus transcriptional and chromatin landscapes (10x Genomics Epi Multiome) on 14,625 primary CD4 + T-cells isolated from treatment-naive early and refractory (defined as per the EULAR definition of difficult-to-treat) patients with RA. We systematically analyze circulating regulatory profiles to reveal potential mechanisms and therapeutic targets that may contribute to the difficult-to-treat phenotype. We highlight disease-stage-specific alterations in naive and Th1-like memory CD4 + T-cells. In particular, refractory naive cells show signatures of heightened activation, upregulation of pathways aligning with T cell anergy, diminished regulation at regulatory loci (e.g., FOXP1, ICOS) and blunted stimulation responses; consistent with a more desensitized or exhausted state. Genes such as LGALS3, ZBTB7B and FOXO4 emerge as potential candidate regulators of the difficult-to-treat state. Finally, through RA GWAS integration, we prioritize putative causal variants in cis-regulatory elements.

items.title: Prostatic granulomatosis with polyangiitis as an uncommon cause of fever of unknown origin: diagnostic pitfalls and a review of reported cases.
items.abstract: Fever of unknown origin (FUO) represents a significant diagnostic challenge in infectious diseases practice, and granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), a rare non-infectious cause of FUO, may lead to diagnostic delay when presenting with prostatic involvement. This study aims to present an atypical case of prostatic GPA and to increase clinical awareness through a focused review of reported cases published after the 2017 International ANCA Consensus. We retrospectively reviewed a 2023 case initially diagnosed as urinary tract infection and subsequently identified as GPA after further evaluation. In addition, a targeted literature search was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, Scopus, Web of Science, and Embase to identify adult cases with biopsy-confirmed prostatic involvement for descriptive analysis. Our patient presented with refractory prostatitis and FUO and was diagnosed with GPA based on PR3-ANCA positivity and multiorgan biopsies. Overall, 19 cases were analyzed, with a mean age of 52.4 ± 16.7 years. FUO with concomitant lower urinary tract symptoms was present in 27.8% (n = 5), PR3-ANCA positivity in 88.9%, skin involvement in 22.2%, and absence of pulmonary involvement in 33.3%. Renal involvement was less frequent (27.8%) than generally reported in GPA. Prolonged unnecessary antibiotic use before diagnosis occurred in 61.1% of cases, and overall survival was 88.9%. Prostatic GPA may mimic refractory urinary infection and contribute to delayed diagnosis. Awareness of this rare prostatic manifestation is important for early diagnosis and improved prognosis.

items.title: Triple immune impairment in an elderly patient with IgG4-AIP and MGUS complicated by dual severe infections over 3 years: A case report.
items.abstract: Reports of IgG4-related autoimmune pancreatitis (IgG4-AIP) combined with monoclonal gammopathy of undetermined significance (MGUS) are mostly limited to short-term follow-up and single infectious complications. To date, no published literature has described octogenarian patients with this overlap complicated by 2 severe concurrent opportunistic infections together with 3-year serial immune-biomarker monitoring. Long-term follow-up data regarding multiple opportunistic infections under continuous immunosuppressive therapy remain scarce for this rare clinical entity. An 82-year-old male patient was diagnosed with IgG4-AIP superimposed by IgGλ-type MGUS. Markedly elevated serum IgG4 (3278.00 μg/mL) and a monoclonal paraprotein level of 2.34 g/L were noted at baseline. Initial combined glucocorticoid-based immunosuppressive therapy partially improved pancreatic lesions. Subsequently, he developed concurrent Staphylococcus hominis bacteremia and active pulmonary tuberculosis. Three-tier superimposed immune impairment, consisting of chronic IgG4-related inflammation, MGUS-associated clonal plasma-cell dysregulation, and drug-induced lymphopenia, was considered the key driver for the dual life-threatening opportunistic infections. Standardized antibacterial and antituberculosis therapeutic regimens were administered to treat the dual infections. Immunosuppressive strategies were adjusted for this high-risk geriatric patient. Complete resolution of infectious lesions was achieved. Over the 36-month longitudinal surveillance period, serum paraprotein remained stable without progression to multiple myeloma, while serum IgG4 concentrations fluctuated independently of MGUS activity. Serial immune profiling confirmed persistent cellular immunodeficiency in this elderly MGUS carrier. This constitutes the first reported octogenarian patient with overlapping IgG4‑AIP and IgGλ‑MGUS suffering from dual severe opportunistic infections following immunosuppressive therapy. Persistent cellular immunodeficiency substantially elevates the risk of life-threatening opportunistic infections in elderly patients with concomitant IgG4-AIP and MGUS. Cyclophosphamide should be used with extreme caution in this vulnerable geriatric subgroup. Pathogenetic mechanisms, infectious risk factors, and preventive considerations for this rare overlapping immune disorder deserve clinical attention.

items.title: Adult-onset Still's disease and sarcopenia-related traits - muscle mass, strength, and function: A bi-directional Mendelian randomization study.
items.abstract: The causal relationship between adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) and sarcopenia remains unclear. Therefore, we employed Mendelian randomization (MR) to investigate the causal link between these 2 conditions. This study investigated the causal relationships between AOSD (n = 201,947) and sarcopenia-related traits, including low handgrip strength (n = 256,523), left handgrip strength (n = 406,552), right handgrip strength (n = 461,089), appendicular lean mass (ALM, n = 450,243), and walking pace (WP, n = 459,915). In the first stage, AOSD served as the exposure variable, while the sarcopenia-related traits treated as the outcome variables; in the second stage, the roles were reversed. MR analysis employed inverse variance-weighted, weighted median, weighted mode, and MR-Egger methods. Cochran's Q statistic was used to assess heterogeneity, while MR-Egger regression and MR-PRESSO were utilized to evaluate pleiotropy. The robustness of the findings, risk of bias, and causal direction were assessed using leave-one-out analysis, funnel plots, and R2 statistics. AOSD may contribute to reduced muscle mass and strength, but not to impaired muscle function. Genetically predicted AOSD is causally associated with reduced ALM (odds ratio [OR] = 0.971, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.951-0.991; P = .005) and increased risk of low hand grip strength in individuals over 60 (OR = 1.046, 95% CI: 1.001-1.091; P = .048). It also reduces left hand grip strength (OR = 0.984, 95% CI: 0.976-0.992; P < .001), with no significant effect on right hand grip strength (OR = 0.995, 95% CI: 0.987-1.003; P = .240). with no effect on WP is also observed (OR = 0.994, 95% CI: 0.988-1.001; P = .080). Genetically predicted sarcopenia-related traits (ALM and bilateral grip strength) had no robust causal effect on AOSD. While inverse variance-weighted suggested nominally significant associations of reduced grip strength (≥60 years) and slower WP with AOSD, these results were inconsistent across MR methods and warrant cautious interpretation. Nominally significant associations observed for low hand grip strength in participants over 60 years and WP were not robust across sensitivity analyses and await further validation.

items.title: Bone marrow sarcoidosis in Takayasu arteritis: Case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is a systemic granulomatous large-vessel vasculitis predominantly involving the aorta and its primary branches. Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous disorder characterized histologically by non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas, most commonly affecting the lungs. Although the coexistence of TA and sarcoidosis has been documented, bone marrow involvement by sarcoidosis in a patient with concomitant TA has not, to our knowledge, been previously reported. A 46-year-old woman with a confirmed diagnosis of TA presented with elevated systemic inflammatory markers and diffuse hypermetabolic activity on positron emission tomography (PET). Clinical, radiological, and pathological evaluations were performed. Bone marrow biopsy revealed multiple non-necrotizing granulomas, supporting bone marrow involvement by sarcoidosis. This overlap of granulomatous conditions was identified in the context of persistent systemic inflammation. Mycofenolate Mofetil was replaced by Infliximab therapy. The patient exhibited significant clinical improvement and marked improvement in inflammatory markers with infliximab therapy. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a broad differential diagnosis in patients with autoimmune or inflammatory diseases who develop new systemic manifestations. Recognizing rare organ involvement in overlapping granulomatous conditions is critical for accurate diagnosis and management.

items.title: Pathological Ossification of Spinal Ligament-Derived Fibroblasts in an Inflammatory Micro-Environment via Activation of the ECM/ITGA5/FAK/AKT Pathway in Ankylosing Spondylitis.
items.abstract: Chronic inflammation and heterotopic ossification (HO) were typical hallmarks of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Although existing target inflammation inhibitors could reduce inflammation but failed to halt HO progression, highlighting the need for osteogenesis-specific treatments. However, the role of fibroblasts (Fbs) responsible for extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling in AS-associated pathological ossification remained unclear. In this study, osteogenic capacity, pathological condition and underlying molecular pathways for Fbs derived from AS spinal ligaments were validated. Fbs from uncalcified spinal ligaments of age-matched AS patients/controls were compared. AS-Fbs were treated with a gradient concentration of TNF-α during osteogenic induction. Meanwhile, specific inhibition of AKT phosphorylation was applied to confirm the role of PI3K/AKT in osteogenesis. Upstream signalling pathways were also explored via RNA-sequencing. Additionally, in vivo, subcutaneous cell transplantation was performed to simulate ectopic ossification. AS-Fbs possessed superior osteogenic capacity than controls. Moreover, osteogenic signs could be promoted by low concentration TNF-α-induced inflammatory micro-environment. Functional analysis revealed a crucial role of the PI3K/AKT pathway. Mechanistically, RNA-seq identified the ECM/integrin subunit alpha 5 (ITGA5)/focal adhesion kinase (FAK) upstream pathway. In detail, osteogenic induction increased ECM protein levels including thrombospondin-1 (THBS1) and fibulin-1 (FBLN1), activating ITGA5, subsequent FAK phosphorylation, osteogenic markers expression and eventually inducing Fb-to-osteocyte differentiation. ITGA5 knockdown or specific FAK inhibition attenuated osteogenic phenotypes and reduced osteogenic proteins expression. Regarding in vivo experiments, subcutaneous bone-like tissue formation derived from transplantation of AS-Fbs was identified and could be suppressed significantly via the AKT phosphorylation inhibition. In conclusion, the findings of this study revealed potential causes for HO progression derived from AS-Fbs in spite of effective anti-inflammation therapy. Furthermore, the crucial role of ECM/ITGA5/FAK/AKT axial signalling pathways in the aberrant osteogenesis of AS-Fbs was identified. Combined targeted intervention at the aforementioned signals and application of anti-inflammatory agents might be a novel potential strategy for the treatment of pathological ectopic ossification caused by AS.

items.title: Predicting Inactive Disease in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis: A Dynamic Machine Learning Approach.
items.abstract: Optimal management of juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) remains challenging. The ability to predict disease progression in JIA can improve personalized treatment decisions, but few reliable predictors have been identified. Using data from the Childhood Arthritis and Rheumatology Research Alliance (CARRA) Registry (years 2015-2024), we developed machine learning models to predict attainment of inactive disease in children with non-systemic JIA. We compared three structurally distinct algorithms: Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBN), Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost). Using a dynamic approach, the models predicted at each timepoint whether a child would attain inactive disease approximately six months later, based on the preceding 12 months of data (demographic, clinical, and medication variables), with predictions updated as new visits accrued. A total of 8,093 participants were included. On an independent test cohort, all 3 models achieved comparable discrimination (AUC 0.76-0.79). Predicted probabilities were well-calibrated (Expected Calibration Error ≤0.03). Disease activity levels in the preceding 12 months, presence of enthesitis and uveitis were the strongest predictors. The dependency structure learned by the DBN indicated that treatment decisions were primarily reactive to disease activity and shaped by JIA category and step-therapy requirements. Machine learning approaches can predict attainment of inactive disease over time with moderate discriminative performance, offering potential to support early identification of children with JIA at risk for unfavorable outcomes. The suboptimal care patterns and systems-level barriers identified through our analyses highlight priority targets for quality improvement initiatives and policy interventions to reduce gaps in JIA care.

items.title: Synovial Tissue-Guided Interleukin-17A Inhibition for Refractory Arthritis in a Patient With Systemic Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis.
items.abstract: The objective of this study was to characterize the clinical, immunologic, and synovial tissue features of a patient with a systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis (sJIA) who carries a novel heterozygous STAT5B loss-of-function variant (p.Gln139Ter) and whose arthritis responded markedly to interleukin-17A (IL-17A) inhibition. Patient blood was compared with blood from healthy donors (n = 5) for immunoblotting, phospho-flow cytometry and immune cell profiling. Patient synovial fluid was compared with synovial fluid from seronegative oligoarticular or polyarticular juvenile idiopathic arthritis (oligo/poly JIA) (n = 5-6) for immune cell profiling. Patient synovial tissue was compared with synovial tissue from children with oligo/poly JIA (n = 11) using Xenium spatial transcriptomics. CD4 + T cells from the patient exhibited impaired STAT5 phosphorylation (z score = -11.1). Synovial fluid CD4 + T cells showed markedly increased IL-17A production (z score = 34.5) and reduced FOXP3 expression (z score = -2.25) in regulatory T cells. Spatial transcriptomics revealed T helper 17 (Th17) cells distributed diffusely throughout the patient's synovium, in contrast to JIA controls in which Th17 cells were largely restricted to tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS) (z score = 3.08). The patient's severe arthritis, previously refractory to IL-1 and IL-6 blockade, improved markedly after IL-17A inhibition. STAT5B haploinsufficiency may contribute to an sJIA phenotype characterized by Th17/IL-17 dysregulation and an altered distribution of Th17 cells outside TLS. Integrated genetic, functional, and spatial tissue analyses may help identify therapeutic targets in refractory pediatric arthritis.

items.title: Evaluation of the efficacy of Si-based agent in Rheumatoid Arthritis with complicating vestibular impairment.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by persistent joint inflammation and progressive disability. Although current therapies have improved clinical outcomes, safer and more effective therapeutic approaches remain needed. Silicon (Si)-based agents have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and have shown beneficial effects in several inflammatory disease models. We evaluated the effects of oral administration of a Si-based agent in a type II collagen-induced arthritis mouse model. Arthritis severity was assessed using an arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and the hindlimb extension reflex test. Serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels were also measured. Vestibular function was evaluated using the vestibulo-ocular reflex (VOR), and inner-ear structural changes were assessed by magnetic resonance imaging and histological analysis. The Si-based agent reduced arthritis-related outcomes, including the arthritis index, hindlimb oedema, and joint movement restriction, and reduced serum type II collagen-specific autoantibody levels. In contrast, no significant differences between the Si-based agent and control groups were detected in VOR-related outcomes, endolymphatic space measurements, or inner-ear histological findings. These findings suggest that the Si-based agent may have beneficial effects on arthritis-related manifestations. However, its effects on the vestibular function-related outcomes examined in this study were not evident. Further studies are needed to clarify the relationship between RA and vestibular dysfunction and to determine the potential therapeutic effects of Si-based agent on these complications.

items.title: Recurrent self-limiting gastroenteritis-like episodes as a diagnostic clue to lupus enteritis in previously undiagnosed systemic lupus erythematosus.
items.abstract: Lupus enteritis may precede recognition of systemic lupus erythematosus. A 40 year-old woman experienced self-limiting episodes of abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea in April and May 2026. Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy in May, as symptoms were subsiding, showed no significant abnormalities; colonoscopy with rectal biopsy was nondiagnostic. In July, recurrent symptoms prompted admission. C-reactive protein was 0.16 mg/dL despite extensive small-bowel wall edema, mesenteric vessel engorgement, ascites, and bilateral urinary tract dilatation without mechanical obstruction on computed tomography. Routine stool culture and Clostridioides difficile toxin testing and culture were negative. High-titer antinuclear antibodies, anti-Sm antibodies, hypocomplementemia, and leukopenia supported a new diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus. The integrated findings favored lupus enteritis with suspected lupus-associated urinary tract involvement. Prednisolone treatment was followed by clinical and radiological improvement. At approximately 12 weeks, there was no clinical relapse, and prednisolone had been tapered to 15 mg/day. This case illustrates how recurrent apparently self-limiting gastrointestinal episodes, nondiagnostic interval endoscopy, a minimal C-reactive protein response despite extensive imaging abnormalities, and unexplained urinary tract dilatation can together prompt recognition of previously undiagnosed systemic lupus erythematosus.

items.title: Trends and Disparities in Mortality with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus as the Underlying Cause Among U.S. Adults, 1999-2023.
items.abstract: To characterize trends, disparities, and forecast trajectories in mortality with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) as the underlying cause among U.S. adults aged ≥ 25 years from 1999 to 2023 while describing differences by sex, age, race/ethnicity, region, and state. We analyzed CDC WONDER Underlying Cause of Death data for ICD-10 codes M32.0, M32.1, M32.8, and M32.9. Crude, age-specific, and age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 were calculated. Archived joinpoint estimates were supplemented by weighted log-linear sensitivity analyses, and seven log-scale forecasting models were compared by rolling-origin validation. The selected model was refitted through 2023 for primary forecasts and through 2019 and 2021 for sensitivity scenarios. Among 28,323 deaths, the AAMR decreased from 0.68 to 0.33 per 100,000 (AAPC, -3.24%). The decline persisted in endpoint-truncated analyses, but the terminal slope attenuated as the minimum segment length increased. AAMRs were higher among females than males; among racial/ethic groups, they were highest in non-Hispanic Black individuals; and among census regions, they were highest in the South. Adults aged 55-64 years contributed the most deaths (5612; 19.8%), whereas the highest observed age-specific rate occurred among adults aged 75-84 years (1.52 per 100,000 in 2001). ARIMA(1,1,0) forecasts remained nonnegative through 2030 but varied when fitted through 2019 or 2021. SLE underlying-cause mortality declined overall, but the recent terminal decline was sensitive to segment assumptions, and demographic and geographic disparities persisted. These population-based rates do not estimate case fatality or mortality risk among people with SLE; forecasts are exploratory.

items.title: Reliability and feasibility of the ankylosing spondylitis performance index (ASPI) in routine clinical care for patients with axial spondyloarthritis.
items.abstract: Patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA) frequently experience limitations in physical function. The performance-based ankylosing spondylitis performance index (ASPI), developed from BASFI items, has demonstrated validity, reliability, and responsiveness in research settings for evaluating physical function. We aimed to assess its reliability and feasibility in routine care. In this prospective observational cohort study, patients with axSpA aged 18-70 years were included if they had a clinical diagnosis of axSpA and were either on a stable NSAID dose for >6 weeks, a stable tumor necrosis factor inhibitor (TNFi) dose for >3 months, or had axSpA without sacroiliitis on X-ray initiating TNFi. ASPI was performed at baseline and 3 months. Test-retest reliability at baseline and 3 months was assessed in the stable treatment group. Feasibility was assessed in all patients using patient-reported outcomes. A total of 39 patients (32 on stable treatment) were included, with a mean age of 44 years, and ~50% women. Bland-Altman analysis revealed low systematic bias (0.1 s), with limits of agreement from -4.4 to 4.6 s. The ASPI composite score showed excellent reliability (ICCs 0.90-0.91). Feasibility was high with a 92% completion rate at baseline; median (IQR) perceived burden score of 5 (2-7) (0 = no burden, 10 = burdensome); and a median score of 10 (1 = unfavorable, 10 = favorable) for annual administration. This study supports the ASPI as a reliable, feasible, and acceptable instrument for evaluating physical function in patients with axSpA. Together with previous evidence on its clinimetric properties, these findings support its potential use as a complementary performance-based measure alongside patient-reported outcomes. Larger studies are needed to evaluate its broader implementation across diverse clinical settings. Key Points • Although the ASPI has demonstrated validity, reliability, and responsiveness in research settings, evidence on its feasibility and reliability in routine clinical care has been limited. • The ASPI showed excellent test-retest reliability in routine care, with intraclass correlation coefficients meeting the threshold for individual-level assessment. • The ASPI was feasible and acceptable from the patient perspective, with high completion rates, clear instructions, and favorable ratings for annual administration. • Together with previous evidence on its clinimetric properties, these findings strengthen the rationale for using the ASPI as a complementary performance-based measure of physical function in routine axSpA care, while larger studies are needed to evaluate its implementation across diverse clinical settings.

items.title: Longitudinal trends in vaccination uptake and respiratory infection burden in systemic lupus erythematosus: a population-based cohort study.
items.abstract: To evaluate longitudinal patterns of vaccination uptake and respiratory infection outcomes among patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) compared with controls and identify factors associated with vaccination uptake. Population-based cohort study using a healthcare organization database. Adult patients with SLE (diagnosed 2010-2023) were identified through a validated registry and matched 1:100 to controls by birth year, sex, and socioeconomic status. Vaccination uptake for influenza, pneumococcal, and COVID-19 vaccines, respiratory infections, hospitalizations, intensive care unit (ICU) admissions, and mortality were evaluated. Temporal trends and factors associated with vaccination uptake were assessed using multivariable models. The study included 3,692 patients with SLE and 382,753 matched controls (median follow-ups 12.8 and 13.4 years, respectively). Vaccination uptake was higher among patients with SLE than controls (influenza: 77.6% vs. 56.4%; pneumococcal: 55.6% vs. 32.1%; COVID-19: 74.2% vs. 72.0%; all p < 0.01). Patients with SLE experienced higher rates of respiratory hospitalization (34.8% vs. 11.5%), pneumonia hospitalization (23.9% vs. 5.9%), ICU admission (12.8% vs. 2.7%), and all-cause mortality (21.0% vs. 8.5%) (all p < 0.001). Longitudinally, vaccination uptake and respiratory hospitalizations remained consistently higher among patients with SLE. Pneumonia hospitalization rates increased over time in controls but remained stable in SLE (interaction p = 0.020). Older age, more comorbidities, higher socioeconomic status, and exposure to glucocorticoids were independently associated with influenza and pneumococcal vaccination uptake rates in SLE. Patients with SLE demonstrated substantially higher vaccine exposure than controls but experienced elevated respiratory infection rates and severe outcomes. These findings support efforts to optimize infection prevention strategies in SLE.

items.title: Association between bosentan and reduced detection of precapillary pulmonary hypertension in systemic sclerosis: evidence from a EUSTAR study.
items.abstract: To evaluate whether exposure to vasoactive-vasodilating drugs (VVDs), particularly bosentan, is associated with reduced detection of precapillary pulmonary hypertension (PH) in systemic sclerosis (SSc). Post hoc retrospective case-control study. European Scleroderma Trials and Research database. SSc patients who underwent their first right heart catheterisation (RHC); patients with postcapillary PH (pulmonary wedge pressure >15 mm Hg) were excluded. Exposure to VVDs (endothelin receptor antagonists (ERAs), phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors, prostanoids) was defined as 'ever' before or 'ongoing' at the time of RHC. Presence of precapillary PH at RHC. Among the 944 patients included in the study, 498 (53%) were diagnosed with precapillary PH. Bosentan 'ever' was associated with a lower likelihood of a precapillary PH detection (OR 0.594, 95% CI 0.362 to 0.975) in the whole population. When considering 'ongoing' bosentan exposure, this result was confirmed only in patients with current DU (OR 0.230, 95% CI 0.081 to 0.652). ERAs in general showed a trend for protective effects towards detection of precapillary PH in patients with current DU ('ever': OR 0.636, 95% CI 0.349 to 1.158; 'ongoing': OR 0.435, 95% CI 0.193 to 1.064), while other VVD classes did not. Bosentan, especially when employed in patients with current DU at the time of RHC, was associated with less detection of precapillary PH. These findings highlight the need for individualised treatment strategies and further research to optimise the timing and patient selection for VVD therapy in SSc.

items.title: VERANDA-SSc: study design of a phase III, randomised, placebo-controlled trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of oral nerandomilast treatment in systemic sclerosis.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a rare, heterogeneous, autoimmune disease. It involves a complex interplay of immune dysregulation, vasculopathy and fibrosis. There are no widely approved drugs that target all three underlying mechanisms and modify the overall SSc disease course or prevent overall disease progression. Nerandomilast, a preferential phosphodiesterase 4B inhibitor, has demonstrated antifibrotic, immunomodulatory and vasculoprotective effects in models relevant to SSc. The phase III VERANDA-SSc trial (NCT07497087) will investigate the efficacy and safety of nerandomilast in patients with SSc. This double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial will be conducted at ~235 sites across 45 countries. Approximately 450 patients with SSc will be randomised 1:1 to receive 18 mg nerandomilast two times a day or placebo in addition to standard-of-care therapy. The dose may be reduced to 9 mg two times a day or interrupted based on individual tolerability or if used concomitantly with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Treatment will continue for at least 52 weeks and until the planned number of primary endpoint events is reached.Adult patients must meet the 2013 American College of Rheumatology/European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology classification criteria, have disease onset within 7 years and have active disease (key inclusion criteria permit the enrolment of patients with diffuse cutaneous or limited cutaneous SSc). items.title: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Giant Cell Arteritis.
items.abstract: Giant cell arteritis (GCA) is a serious systemic vasculitis that can lead to irreversible complications, if not promptly recognized and treated. Global estimates of GCA incidence and prevalence show considerable variation, reflecting differences in diagnostic criteria, geographic context, and evolving clinical practices. This study updates prior meta-analyses of GCA epidemiology, which predate widespread use of contemporary diagnostic approaches. The objective was to systematically review and meta-analyze population-based studies reporting GCA incidence and prevalence worldwide and explore sources of heterogeneity. A systematic search of PubMed, MEDLINE, Embase, and Scopus was performed from inception to October 2025. Studies were included if they reported population-based incidence or prevalence of GCA in adults ≥50 years. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed using the restricted maximum likelihood estimator for τ 2 , and meta-regressions were used to explore potential sources of heterogeneity. A total of 5,465 records were screened, and 54 studies from 23 countries were included. Pooled crude annual incidence was 10.59 per 100,000 persons ≥50 years (95% confidence interval [CI] 7.69-13.48; I 2  = 99.89%, τ 2  = 67.33, Q (31) = 16,434.60; P < 0.001), whereas pooled prevalence was 67.68 per 100,000 persons ≥50 years (95% CI 34.15-101.20; I 2  = 99.97%). Incidence increased with absolute latitude. The number of case-ascertainment methods and data sources showed no association. The highest incidence estimates came from Northern Europe and the highest prevalence estimates from North America. Pooled incidence was approximately two-fold higher in female patients.

items.title: Percutaneous device closure of a massive pseudoaneurysm of the descending aorta in a paediatric patient with Takayasu arteritis.
items.abstract: Takayasu arteritis (TA) is commonly known as a disease of young women, highly prevalent in Asia and Central America, and associated with multiple vascular complications. Although it is well described in the paediatric population, severe complications are rarely seen. A 6-year-old girl was referred to our institution with features suggestive of a tuberculosis infection, along with a suspected intrathoracic mass on preliminary imaging. Further investigations confirmed the mass to be a massive pseudoaneurysm originating from the descending aorta and extending into the left hemithorax. A multidisciplinary discussion concluded that this pseudoaneurysm carried a high mortality risk with a direct surgical approach. This case report describes the use of an Amplatzer TM septal occluder as a bridge to surgical excision of the massive pseudoaneurysm in a paediatric patient with confirmed TA.

items.title: Pseudo-pseudo Meigs Syndrome as the first clinical manifestation of systemic lupus erythematosus after controlled ovarian stimulation for ICSI: a case report.
items.abstract: Pseudo-pseudo Meigs syndrome (PPMS), or Tjalma syndrome, is a rare systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)-associated phenotype characterized by ascites, pleural effusion, and elevated CA125 without an ovarian neoplasm. After assisted reproductive technology (ART), it may overlap with ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS) or mimic gynecologic malignancy. A 25-year-old woman underwent two controlled ovarian stimulation (COS) cycles for intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) because of severe male-factor infertility. Before ART, she had autoimmune thyroid disease and transient urinary abnormalities, but no known SLE. During the second COS cycle, hypertension and albuminuria emerged. Following oocyte retrieval, she developed massive ascites, bilateral pleural effusions, adnexal abnormalities, and marked CA125 elevation, initially raising suspicion of OHSS and ovarian malignancy. Subsequent nephrotic-range proteinuria, profound hypoalbuminemia, hypocomplementemia, and SLE-associated autoantibodies supported active SLE with substantial renal involvement. Cytologic and microbiologic investigations provided no evidence of malignancy or infection. Following SLE-directed treatment, renal abnormalities and serosal effusions improved. At eight months, the adnexal abnormalities had completely resolved and CA125 had normalized, supporting a PPMS phenotype. Atypical or persistent post-ART effusions, particularly when accompanied by evolving renal or immunologic abnormalities, should prompt consideration of SLE-associated PPMS as an important differential diagnosis beyond OHSS and gynecologic malignancy. Longitudinal evaluation and multidisciplinary assessment may facilitate timely recognition of this rare phenotype and guide appropriate clinical management.

items.title: Short echo time first-echo images of T2* mapping for detecting structural sacroiliac joint lesions in axial spondyloarthritis: a CT-referenced study.
items.abstract: To assess the CT-referenced diagnostic performance of short-echo time (TE) first-echo images derived from a T2* mapping acquisition for detecting sacroiliac joint (SIJ) structural lesions in patients evaluated for axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA), compared with conventional T1-weighted turbo spin-echo (T1-TSE) MRI. In this study, 54 patients underwent SIJ CT and 3T MRI; 52 were included in the final analysis. MRI included T1-TSE and a T2* mapping acquisition; the first-echo magnitude images (TE = 4.36 ms) were used for structural assessment. Two blinded readers scored CT and MRI using the Berlin and SPARCC structural scoring systems. Patient-level sensitivity (SE), specificity (SP), and diagnostic accuracy (DA) were calculated using CT as the reference. Correlation with CT was assessed using Pearson's r, and inter-rater agreement was evaluated (κ for Berlin binary positivity; ICC for continuous sum scores). Forty-three of 52 patients fulfilled ASAS 2009/2011 spondyloarthritis classification criteria. Compared with T1-TSE, short TE-T2* images showed higher diagnostic performance for erosions (SE 88.6% vs 51.4%; SP 70.6% vs 82.4%; DA 82.6% vs 61.7%) and sclerosis (SE 86.2% vs 34.5%; SP 95.7% vs 100%; DA 90.3% vs 62.4%), while both sequences achieved high accuracy for joint space changes (DA 98.2%; T2*: SE/SP 98%/100%; T1: 100%/66.7%). Agreement with CT was stronger for short TE-T2* than for T1-TSE for Berlin erosion and sclerosis sum scores (r=0.913 and 0.921 vs 0.646 and 0.758), with substantial reader agreement for erosion and sclerosis positivity (κ=0.805 and 0.731 vs 0.564 and 0.598). Short TE first echo images from a T2* mapping acquisition provide an accessible, radiation-free, erosion-sensitive approach that demonstrates higher CT-referenced detection of erosions and sclerosis compared with conventional T1-TSE imaging, with strong CT agreement and robust inter-rater reliability.

items.title: Multi-omics profiling identifies a putative Akkermansia -HK3-lactate immunometabolic link associated with JPZS treatment in lupus nephritis.
items.abstract: Lupus nephritis (LN) is associated with aberrant glycolytic reprogramming in renal immune cells, yet its relationship with gut microbial alterations remains poorly defined. Hexokinase 3 (HK3) has emerged as a candidate metabolic node in myeloid activation, while the relationship between gut Akkermansia abundance and renal HK3-associated metabolic changes in LN remains unclear. We used Qihuang Jianpi Zishen decoction (JPZS), an herbal formula used as an adjunct in clinical practice, as an experimental probe to investigate this putative gut-immunometabolic connection through integrated multi-omics. Female MRL/lpr mice ( n = 6 per group) received JPZS (6.305, 12.61, or 25.22 g/kg/day) or vehicle for 8 weeks, with C57BL/6 mice serving as a healthy reference group. Renal function, autoantibodies, histopathology, and glomerular IgG deposition were assessed across treatment groups. Integrated multi-omics profiling-fecal 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted plasma metabolomics, and renal RNA sequencing-was performed in the matched control, model, and high-dose JPZS groups. Renal lactate and pyruvate were quantified, and HK3 and Ldhal6b mRNA and their corresponding proteins were evaluated by qPCR and western blotting. HK3/F4/80 dual immunofluorescence was additionally performed to examine the spatial localization of HK3 relative to renal macrophages. JPZS reduced proteinuria, serum creatinine, glomerular IgG deposition, and renal histopathological injury in MRL/lpr mice. Gut microbiome profiling showed marked enrichment of Akkermansia and altered community composition, without significant recovery of Chao1 or Shannon diversity, accompanied by reductions in Klebsiella and Enterococcus . Plasma metabolomics revealed remodeling of amino-acid and central carbon metabolism, while renal transcriptomics identified immune-related differences and an exploratory glycolysis/gluconeogenesis enrichment signal. JPZS reduced renal lactate accumulation and the lactate/pyruvate ratio and decreased renal HK3 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels. Dual immunofluorescence showed increased HK3 and F4/80 fluorescence in model kidneys, with overlapping signals evident in merged images; both signals were lower following JPZS-H treatment. Cross-layer correlation analyses linked gut genera, circulating metabolites, and renal gene expression; targeted assays separately characterized renal lactate/pyruvate status. JPZS ameliorated renal injury while inducing coordinated changes in the gut microbiome, circulating metabolome, and renal immunometabolic profile in MRL/lpr mice. Integrated multi-omics and targeted validation identified a putative Akkermansia -HK3-lactate immunometabolic link associated with JPZS treatment. These findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for gut-kidney immunometabolic crosstalk in LN and warrant future causal validation through microbiota- and HK3-targeted approaches.

items.title: Evodiamine attenuates hyperuricemia-associated gouty arthritis and renal injury through urate-inflammatory axis modulation.
items.abstract: Therapeutic options for hyperuricemia (HUA) and its complications remain inadequate, particularly when gouty arthritis (GA) and hyperuricemic nephropathy (HN) coexist. Agents with combined urate-lowering, anti-inflammatory, and renoprotective effects are therefore needed. Evodiamine (EVO), a major alkaloid from Evodia rutaecarpa , exhibits anti-inflammatory and analgesic activities, but its role in HUA-related disorders has not been fully defined. We examined the effects of Evodia rutaecarpa water extract (ERWE) and EVO in experimental models of HUA, HN, and GA. In the HUA model, ERWE reduced plasma UA levels and increased urinary UA concentration, accompanied by reductions in ALT, AST, and selected inflammatory measurements. Metabolomic profiling indicated that these effects were associated with alterations in pyrimidine metabolism, α-linolenic acid metabolism, and butyrate-related pathways. In the HN model, EVO lowered serum UA and creatinine levels, improved renal pathology, and reduced renal URAT1 and GLUT9 expression. EVO also suppressed NLRP3/caspase-1/IL-1β signaling and reduced the expression of fibrosis-related markers, including α-SMA, COL1A1, and TIMP1. In the GA model, EVO alleviated monosodium urate (MSU)-induced ankle swelling, leukocyte infiltration, and inflammatory mediator production, including IL-1β, TNF-α, and MPO, while inhibiting NLRP3 inflammasome activation. ERWE and the alkaloid EVO showed significant protective effects in experimental HUA-related disorders. EVO, in particular, exerted urate-lowering, renoprotective, and anti-inflammatory activities, possibly through regulation of urate transporters and NLRP3 inflammasome signaling.

items.title: Presumed Paravertebral Inflammatory Pseudotumor in Relapsing Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis: Fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (PET/CT) Findings and Complete Metabolic Response to Rituximab-Based Therapy.
items.abstract: We report a case of a 60-year-old woman with biopsy-proven, proteinase-3 (PR3)-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)-associated granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), diagnosed six years earlier, who presented with right lower thoracic pain during a disease relapse. The relapse was supported by serological reactivation with a markedly elevated anti-PR3 level, a raised erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) (88 mm/h), and elevated C-reactive protein (CRP) (48 mg/L). Unenhanced computed tomography (CT) showed no pulmonary parenchymal abnormality but revealed soft-tissue infiltration of the anterior and right lateral paravertebral mediastinal fat extending from T4-T5 to T10-T11, without adjacent osseous involvement. Fluorine-18 ( 18 F)-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG) positron emission tomography/CT (PET/CT) demonstrated intense uptake within the lesion, with a maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) of 12.06. Given the differential diagnoses of lymphoma and other granulomatous disease, the lesion was interpreted as a presumed GPA-related paravertebral inflammatory pseudotumor; it was not biopsied. After rituximab and methylprednisolone, the patient achieved complete clinical and biological remission with ANCA seroconversion, and follow-up FDG PET/CT at three months showed complete resolution of the abnormal uptake. Because neither FDG avidity nor treatment response was specific, the presumed diagnosis could not be confirmed histologically in this case.

items.title: Peripartum cardiomyopathy and antiphospholipid syndrome: a rare association revealed by a right ventricular thrombus. A case report.
items.abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is uncommon, and its association with antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) and right ventricular (RV) thrombus is exceptional. We report a 33-year-old woman who, three months after cesarean delivery for severe preeclampsia, developed acute heart failure with severe biventricular dysfunction requiring mechanical ventilation. An RV thrombus was identified; two computed tomographic pulmonary angiograms, one week apart, were negative for pulmonary embolism. Thrombophilia work-up disclosed persistently positive lupus anticoagulant on repeat testing 12 weeks apart, supporting APS. Therapeutic anticoagulation led to complete thrombus resolution after 10 days, and optimized heart failure therapy was followed by hemodynamic improvement and successful extubation. Coronary angiography ruled out ischemic heart disease, and endomyocardial biopsy showed no histologic evidence of myocarditis, supporting PPCM. Myocardial recovery was partial, requiring follow-up within an advanced heart failure program. This case highlights the need to evaluate secondary prothrombotic conditions, particularly APS, and to institute early anticoagulation in PPCM with intracardiac thrombosis. La miocardiopatía periparto (PPCM) es infrecuente y su asociación con el síndrome antifosfolipídico (SAF) y trombo en el ventrículo derecho (VD) es excepcional. Presentamos el caso de una mujer de 33 años quien, tres meses después de una cesárea indicada por preeclampsia severa, presentó insuficiencia cardíaca aguda con disfunción biventricular grave, que requirió ventilación mecánica invasiva. Se identificó un trombo en el VD; para descartar tromboembolismo pulmonar, se realizaron dos angiotomografías pulmonares con un intervalo de una semana, ambas negativas. Se realizó un estudio de trombofilias, diagnosticándose SAF. Se instauró anticoagulación terapéutica, con resolución del trombo a los 10 días. La coronariografía descartó cardiopatía isquémica y la biopsia endomiocárdica no encontró evidencia de miocarditis; el diagnóstico fue PPCM. La recuperación miocárdica fue parcial, requiriendo seguimiento en el programa de falla cardíaca avanzada. Este caso subraya la importancia de la evaluación sistemática de SAF y la pronta anticoagulación en PPCM con trombosis intracardiaca.

items.title: Adult-onset Still's Disease.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a rare auto inflammatory condition characterized by high fever, joint pain, a transient salmon-colored rash, and elevated ferritin levels. Its diagnosis is primarily clinical, relying on the exclusion of infections, malignancies, and other autoimmune disorders. A 23-year-old woman presented with intermittent high fever, polyarthralgia, and a fleeting salmon-pink rash. Laboratory results showed neutrophilic leukocytosis, elevated ESR, CRP, and ferritin (1650 ng/mL), along with mild liver enzyme elevation and negative ANA/RF tests. Extensive investigations for infections and cancer were inconclusive. She met the Yamaguchi criteria for Adult-onset Still's disease. The patient responded well to oral prednisolone and methotrexate. After a relapse at 7 months, treatment was adjusted with increased methotrexate doses, a short course of steroids, and NSAIDs. At a one-year follow-up, she remains symptom-free, with normalized ferritin levels (280 ng/mL) and no signs of macrophage activation syndrome (MAS). Adult-onset Still's disease should be considered in patients with fever of unknown origin accompanied by systemic inflammation. Early recognition and immunosuppressive therapy can lead to remission, even in settings with limited resources.
